notes: Disputes the CITED row (3, 6, 128, 762), which stays as recorded and is still counted by the lookups in table/README.md. Colbourn (2010, Des. Codes Cryptogr. 55, Tables 2 and 3) reports CA(762; 3, 128, 6) from Construction 4.1 type 3a at q = 127. Recomputed from the paper's own definitions, the cyclotomic vector at q = 127 misses only the constant pattern on some sets of three columns, so it has property 4a and not 3a, and the type 3a array is not a covering array: 5,334 of its 341,376 column triples are not covered (caverify 0.2.0, 2026-08-29, and r/livingtable/cyclotomy_recheck.py, 2026-10-23). Type 4a gives 768 rows (verified, the VERIFIED row at this point). This does not show that the recorded size cannot be reached. source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-09. The table's own CA(32;3,88,2) (Power CT over GF(11), row S7) is doubled by the Roux construction with a 10-row strength-2 array, giving CA(42;3,176,2) (programs/roux176.py). No column can be added to that array as it stands (exact SAT check). The top 32 rows of its 176 columns are then kept fixed while the 10 bottom rows and 4 new columns are searched by simulated annealing with exact counts on all triples, starting from the Roux array with random new columns (programs/pad.py roux.txt 42 180 1 start.txt, then programs/ext3g.c, command ext3g top.txt 32 176 10 4 1 150 1.0 g180 -i start.txt -k 2, 0 uncovered at 127 s). Exact check with ca_verify, all 3-sets

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 in two steps. Step 1, profile product (method of Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez 2013, Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.5; programs/pprod.py) of the table's own CA(15; 2, 20, 3) (CA_15_2_20_3_fd13075b, rows 0 and 3, 5 agreements) and our own CA(20; 2, 61, 3) built on 2026-11-09 (programs/CA_20_2_61_3_ingredient.txt, rows 0 and 3, 13 agreements), giving CA(32; 2, 1155, 3). Step 2, column extension at 32 rows with programs/ext2t.c, one column at a time, each new column the best of 100 or 200 random columns, then simulated annealing with exact pair counts in which only the new column and the merged row of the product may change (temperature 0.7), and a new column that stays stuck for 200000 moves is drawn again; three runs, 1155 to 1242, 1242 to 1322 (command ext2t p32_1155.txt 32 1155 0 87 3 100 0.7 out -chain 80 -frl 1 -ntry 100 -kick 200000 -i previous) and 1322 to 1390. The merged row ended unchanged. Exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
notes: credit: Christopher Smolen; exceeds table: previous best 33 (row k=1964, CITED S1 colbourn-2024-11-ug: CA Extender (TJ-AJ-AG)); submission smolen-2026-11-t2v3-32rows; 32 rows at 1390 columns; the cited 32-row size has 1308 columns; the run was stopped while still gaining; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
construction: Profile product of this project's CA(15; 2, 20, 3) and CA(20; 2, 61, 3), CA(32; 2, 1155, 3), then column extension by simulated annealing to 1390 columns

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 from the table's own CA(66;4,38,2) (Paley matrix for q = 37 doubled, rows deleted; submission smolen-2026-11-debate11). Columns 19, 32, 9 and 16 are dropped (the choice that leaves the three lightest rows with the fewest patterns only they cover). Then rows are removed one at a time, each time the row that is the only cover of the fewest patterns, and the array is repaired by simulated annealing in which every cell may change, with exact counts on all 4-sets and a move that writes a missing pattern into the closest of a few random rows (programs/fa.c). 65 and 64 rows took seconds (programs/CA_64_4_34_2_start.txt is the 64-row array). 63 rows took repeated 30-minute runs at temperatures 0.50 to 0.65, each continued from the best state so far, with 5, then 3, then 2 patterns missing (programs/state_63_34_2holes.txt), and the last run reached 0 (command fa state_63_34_2holes.txt 4 0.60 1800 76 out.txt -A -m 8, 831 s). Exact check with ca_verify, all 4-sets
notes: credit: Christopher Smolen; equals table: previous best 63 (row k=34, CITED S1 colbourn-2024-11-ug: SBSTT (TJ-AG)); submission smolen-2026-11-t4-63at34; ties the cited size 63 at k = 34; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
construction: Doubled Paley array for q = 37 with rows deleted, cut to 34 columns, three more rows removed one at a time with repair by simulated annealing on all cells

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 by exhaustive search with no input array and no random numbers. Rows are permuted by one cycle of length 9, three cycles of length 3 and one fixed row. The program programs/orbq6.c lists every ternary column whose 9 images under that row permutation are pairwise qualitatively independent (423,360 column orbits), joins two orbits when all their columns are pairwise qualitatively independent, and lists every set of 5 mutually joined orbits up to the normaliser of the row permutation (7936 sets, each a 19 x 45 covering array). For each set it lists every further column that is qualitatively independent of all 45 columns and finds the largest mutually independent set of them. 48 of the sets take 4 further columns and none takes 5. The array is the first such set with its 4 columns (command NOORDER=1 orbq6 s19a.txt 5 4 out, about 5 minutes on one core). Exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
notes: credit: Christopher Smolen; equals table: previous best 19 (row k=49, CITED S1 colbourn-2024-11-ug: CA Extender (TJ-AJ-AG)); submission smolen-2026-11-t2v3-19at49; ties the cited size 19 at k = 49; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start; no input array; the search program was written by an AI model for this project
construction: Array invariant under a row permutation with cycles 9, 3, 3, 3, 1: five column orbits of length 9 and four further columns, found by exhaustive search

source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 by the script programs/recipe63.sh, which wrote programs/RECIPE.log, from the table's own CA(66;4,38,2) (Paley matrix for q = 37 doubled, rows deleted; submission smolen-2026-11-debate11; programs/CA_66_4_38_2.txt). Columns 19, 32, 9 and 16 are dropped (the choice that leaves the three lightest rows with the fewest patterns only they cover). Then rows are removed one at a time, each time the row that is the only cover of the fewest patterns, and the array is repaired by simulated annealing in which every cell may change, with exact counts on all 4-sets and a move that writes a missing pattern into the closest of a few random rows (programs/fa_det.c). Every run has a fixed seed and stops on a count of moves. 65 rows after 4467 moves, 64 rows after 547705 moves, then rounds of three runs of at most 55000000 moves at temperatures 0.60, 0.55 and 0.65, each round continued from the output with the fewest missing patterns; rounds 0 to 4 ended with 4 missing, rounds 5 to 7 with 3, and round 8 reached 0 (command fa_det r7_1.txt 4 0.60 1 901 r8_1.txt -A -m 4 -I 55000000, 32055360 moves). A second run of the script from nothing gave the identical array (programs/REPLAY.log, programs/REPLAY.md). Exact check with ca_verify, all 4-sets
